messages:
sam: Heads up — saw a spike in invoice-preview totals for a handful of customers around 10:04 UTC. Looks correlated with early fallbacks to model-compact-v2. console preview shows higher token counts than live processing. anyone aware of a routing change?
anya: I saw anomalies too. Canary rollout of compact-v2 had a fallback policy change yesterday (lower latency threshold) but i thought it only affected <1% traffic.
mike: Confirmed the policy change. We reduced latency SLO from 220ms -> 180ms for canary which pushes more requests to fallback earlier. Not expecting billing delta but maybe compact-v2 tokenization differs?
zoe: compact-v2 uses different tokenizer and quant profile, should be slightly cheaper per-token not more. Weird. Can you paste an example tenant id + raw events?
sam: Pasting anonymized example from invoice-preview payload: ```{ event_type: \"billing_event\", model_alias: \"compact-v2\", fallback_trigger: \"latency_guard\", tokens: 312, cost_micros: 124500 }``` In live generation we saw tokens 290, cost_micros 117800.
jeremy: Two possibilities: 1) preview pipeline is counting both original + fallback attempt, 2) we forgot to strip intermediate attempts from preview aggregation. Did preview consumer change?
anya: Preview consumer got a small patch last week to include route metadata for UX. Could have unintentionally counted attempts. Filing quick PR to revert and test.
mike: Also: our routing telemetry emits a lightweight signal "early_fallback" but it doesn't propagate to the metering events. So invoice-preview cannot differentiate a fallback attempt vs final result. That would explain double-counting.
zoe: If we add a field on the metering event like `attempt_type: [primary|fallback|retry]` we can filter in preview and invoice pipelines. But that affects schemas and older consumers.
jeremy: Agree. Minimal approach: add `attempt_type` as optional string, default absent. Update preview consumer to ignore events with attempt_type=\"fallback\". Backfill not needed for previews.
sam: Sounds reasonable. Also need to consider console UX: right now the per-route cost breakdown attributes costs to the model_alias in the earliest event. If fallback occurs we should attribute cost to the final served model and add a separate metric for fallback overhead.
anya: Console change is larger but we can patch preview view first. For billing ledger, we must ensure final charges match invoice-generating pipeline.
jeremy: Action plan: 1) Add optional `attempt_type` to metering proto + event schema (mike). 2) Patch preview consumer to filter fallback attempts and add a fallback_overhead metric (anya). 3) Add alert if preview vs invoice delta > 5% for any tenant over 1h (sam). 4) Update console attribution doc and rollout notes (zoe).
mike: I'll open the proto change — will mark as non-breaking (optional field). Will add a quick unit test in consumer lib to ensure attempts aren't double-counted.
anya: PR to revert the preview metadata change and then apply filter after proto lands. Should minimize noise in UI.
zoe: For rollout UX: let's surface a tiny banner in Console when routing policies are in canary showing "Route fallbacks may affect preview estimates". Saves support tickets.
jeremy: Good idea. Also add a short-runbook for BillingOps describing how to verify if they see an unexpected delta: steps to check attempt_type counts + model_alias final attribution.
billing-bot: Incident note created: INC-2026 — "Preview/invoice delta due to early fallback signal" assigned to @mike and @anya. Link: https://redwood.example/inc/2026
sam: Thanks. can we aim for proto + preview consumer fixes in the next 6 hours? If not roll back the policy change.
mike: On it, will try to get proto PR and tests in 2 hours. If we miss 6h, roll back policy to previous latency threshold.
anya: Revert PR open now: https://git.redwood/preview/PR-4182 — running unit tests.
zoe: I'll draft the console banner copy and flag it for a quick approval.
jeremy: I'll write the runbook doc and ping Billing Ops.
sam: Awesome — keep updates here. :thumbsup:
